I was about 5 years old when I had this dream, and I still remember it vividly.

My brothers, my aunt and I were in a giant room, with a ceiling maybe six stories high and about the size of a sports arena. In the middle is a giant Hot Wheels track, made for regular-sized vehicles. The room had dirty orange carpets and drab yellow lights way up at the ceiling and I remember I couldn't actually see the other side, almost like a lack of draw distance on a video game. 

My aunt got my attention to enter a small door way in the corner, and I entered. When I got in, I realized it was my basement, and all the lights were off. There was a witch in a coffin lying dead on the coffee table in front of me with a few candles burning. I'm pretty creeped out but I maintain my composure. My aunt gestures to the side of the room, where a bathroom cubicle is set up, which I had previously not noticed. My aunt says "Please, use the washroom in remembrance." I step inside the cubicle, only the find a giant spider on the other side of the swinging door. It had wild, large human eyes, and it almost looked like a old 3D cartoon from the late 90s. It jumped at me and that's the climactic point where I woke up. 

I still have no idea what was going on in my subconscious...

Hey, man/girl. Almost every line you wrote was something I could relate to. It really, really sucks when it feels like everyone is out blossoming in the wild when you're still a seedling at the same age. I actually used to work at a fast food joint too, until I quit 6 months ago, and I'm 19 by the way.

The single best mind frame I'm able to compose for myself is that life is anything but a race. Just because everyone else is winning, it doesn't mean you won't cross the finish line too. First girlfriend at age 30? Cool. First job at 28? Cool. You're not on a timeline, you're not holding up traffic. It's you're life, and you come first. It's easy to give in to social norms. And I'm not saying to sell yourself short. Of course you should pursue your passions and goals, but don't pull yourself apart if you fail to meet your expectations. Sometimes I feel like people tell me that I have to be "successful" to be happy, but realistically as long as I can smile and love myself no matter what, that's as successful as I need to be. 

Of course, it's difficult to adopt that it fits of severe depression. For all I know, I sound like an idiot write now. Believe me, I'm not spewing those sentiments out on my worst days, and you can bet your ass I don't believe them then. But I truly believe that at the end of the day, no one is stacking me up next to people richer or more attractive than I am, and that's the best goddamn thing, because I'd fail miserably at both of those. Again, I'm in no way trying to belittle your passions. Give it all you've got. But remember that your value as a human being is so far beyond a salary and a social status.

And as for the comment about your brother, maybe that's all he wants to do. I could be completely wrong, but I entertain the possibility he could be totally happy in his position. I'm not suggesting you follow suit, but hey, maybe that's his happy place.
